# Compound Trigger Over Package State

**Decision.** Implement a statement-spanning trigger rule as a **single compound trigger** rather than
as three separate triggers sharing variables in a package — and keep the rejected implementation in
the tree, labelled.

**Date.** 2026-07-25 (evidence date), `sql/03_plsql/04_triggers.sql` of
[[oracle-database-laboratories]].

## The problem both versions solve

The rule needs the chief's ration read **once before any row changes**, plus running totals
accumulated **across every affected row**, then a settlement write after the statement completes. A
row-level trigger can hold neither; a statement-level trigger cannot see per-row values. See
[[database-triggers]] and the mutating-table restriction it describes.

## Version (a): three triggers plus a package

`BEFORE STATEMENT` initialises package variables, `BEFORE EACH ROW` accumulates into them,
`AFTER STATEMENT` settles up and writes back. It works, and the file says exactly where it is thin:

> "This works, but it is fragile in a way worth naming: the AFTER STATEMENT trigger updates
> Cats.mice_ration, which is the very column its own BEFORE UPDATE OF trigger watches, so it
> re-enters the trigger chain. The guard flag below is what stops that recursion. Version (b) has no
> such problem and is the one to prefer."
> — Oracle-Database-Laboratories/sql/03_plsql/04_triggers.sql, 2026-07-25

Two failure modes, not one. The **re-entrancy** is stopped only by a hand-managed `settling` boolean
that every one of the three triggers must check — remove it from any of them and the chain recurses.
And the state is **package state**: it persists for the session, so a statement that ends abnormally
leaves the totals dirty for the next one, which is why the `BEFORE STATEMENT` trigger has to zero
them by hand.

## Version (b): one compound trigger

> "The compound trigger: one object, four timing points, state held in the trigger's own declaration
> section. No package, no globals leaking between statements, and the state is reinitialised
> automatically for each statement -- which is what the package version had to do by hand."
> — Oracle-Database-Laboratories/sql/03_plsql/04_triggers.sql, 2026-07-25

Three defects removed by one construct: no shared global, no manual reinitialisation, and — because
the settlement `UPDATE` happens in `AFTER STATEMENT` of the same object rather than in a separate
trigger watching the same column — no re-entrancy and therefore no guard flag.

## Alternatives rejected

| Option | Why not |
|---|---|
| **Three triggers + package variables** | re-entrant; needs a hand-managed guard flag; session-scoped state must be zeroed by hand — *stated in the repo* |
| **Do the work in application code instead** | not considered in the repo; the rule is a database invariant and the exercise is trigger design |

**TODO:** the second row is not evidenced. Only the three-trigger alternative is recorded as
considered and rejected.

## Why the inferior version stays in the tree

Deliberately, and it is the interesting part of this decision. Both implementations sit in the same
file, in order, with the trade-off written between them — this is
[[keep-the-superseded-version-in-tree]] used **pedagogically** rather than archivally, and the local
instance of [[multiple-solutions-side-by-side]]. Deleting version (a) would leave a compound trigger
with no visible reason to exist.

The cost is the usual one for duplication: two implementations of the same rule that must be kept in
agreement, in a repository with no tests. They currently agree.
